1051	    /// The rules a media's `speech` obeys, each failure its own sentence
1052	    /// naming the media and the span. A media without `speech` passes.
1053	    pub(crate) fn check_media_speech(&self, media: &Media) -> Result<(), String> {
1054	        let Some(spans) = &media.speech else {
1055	            return Ok(());
1056	        };
1057	        let id = media.id;
1058	        if !media.has_audio {
1059	            return Err(format!(
1060	                "media {id} has no audio, so it has no speech to duck by"
1061	            ));
1062	        }
1063	        if spans.len() > MAX_SPEECH_SPANS {
1064	            return Err(format!(
1065	                "media {id} carries {} speech spans, more than {MAX_SPEECH_SPANS}",
1066	                spans.len()
1067	            ));
1068	        }
1069	        let mut previous: Option<Ticks> = None;
1070	        for (i, &[start, end]) in spans.iter().enumerate() {
1071	            if start < 0 {
1072	                return Err(format!(
1073	                    "media {id} speech span {i} starts at {start}, before 0"
1074	                ));
1075	            }
1076	            if end <= start {
1077	                return Err(format!(
1078	                    "media {id} speech span {i} ends at {end}, not after its start {start}"
1079	                ));
1080	            }
1081	            if end > media.duration {
1082	                return Err(format!(
1083	                    "media {id} speech span {i} ends at {end}, past the media's duration {}",
1084	                    media.duration
1085	                ));
1086	            }
1087	            if let Some(before) = previous.filter(|before| start < *before) {
1088	                return Err(format!(
1089	                    "media {id} speech span {i} starts at {start}, before span {} ends at \
1090	                     {before}: speech spans are sorted and do not overlap",
1091	                    i - 1
1092	                ));
1093	            }
1094	            previous = Some(end);
1095	        }
1096	        Ok(())
1097	    }

1275	                // (`edit_props.rs`'s `snap_animation`, and the Times rule

1289	                scale: 1.0,

1305	        shape: Option<&Value>,
1306	    ) -> Result<Outcome, String> {

1308	            None => ShapeProps::default(),

1314	                // `ShapeProps::default()`: that default is also the base a
1315	                // stored shape is deserialized against and the value a
1316	                // later `set_shape { "kind": "arrow" }` merges into, and a
1317	                // patch that re-paints a field the caller did not name
1318	                // would break the merge contract. Merging the patch over
1319	                // this preset (not under it) keeps an explicit
1320	                // `"arrow_end": false` winning.
1321	                let kind = patch
1322	                    .get("kind")
1323	                    .and_then(|value| serde_json::from_value(value.clone()).ok());

1326	                    ..ShapeProps::default()
1327	                };

1331	            }

1334	        // oversized footage does.

1337	            track,
1338	            at,
1339	            duration,
1340	            Described {
1341	                source: Source::Shape,
1342	                scale,
1343	                text: None,
1344	                shape: Some(props),
1345	                graphic: None,
1346	            },

1	//! Adjustment clips (spec §11 GR-6): a clip kind with no picture of its
2	//! own. While it lasts, its `video.color` (all thirteen keys), its wheels
3	//! (spec §11 GR-11), its curves (GR-12), its look, its point filters (sepia, noir, vignette,
4	//! invert) and its opacity — the STRENGTH —
5	//! apply to everything already drawn behind it in its container (to the
6	//! pixels its qualifier selects, GR-13), the canvas
7	//! background included, and never to a track in front. The compositor's
8	//! eighth pipeline does the grading by reading the target it draws into
9	//! (`Compositor+Adjustment.swift`); the core's part is the kind, the op,
10	//! the rules below and the recipe's `{"kind":"adjustment"}` source.
11	//!
12	//! What it refuses, and why each is a refusal rather than a clamp:
13	//!
14	//! - **A nest.** A nest is flattened into the clips inside it, and an
15	//!   adjustment clip in there would grade the PARENT's layers behind the
16	//!   nest clip as well as the nest's own, which is not what a nest means.
17	//!   `nest` refuses it ([`adjustment_cannot_nest`]); `validate` errors on one
18	//!   inside a nest ([`adjustment_nested`]), which is what a file and a paste
19	//!   into a scope meet, because a scoped edit is validated on the MERGED
20	//!   parent (`scope.rs`); and `add_adjustment_clip` has no meaning inside a
21	//!   scope (`scope.rs`'s `refused_inside`).
22	//! - **A transition.** Both halves of a dissolve are drawn into one
23	//!   destination as a weighted pair; a pass that grades the destination has
24	//!   no half to be. `add_transition`, `set_transition` and
25	//!   `set_transition_style` refuse ([`adjustment_transition`]), and so does
26	//!   the overlap rule for any pair that holds one
27	//!   ([`adjustment_overlap`], called from `transition.rs`'s
28	//!   `check_overlap_rule`, the one placement door) — so
29	//!   `set_gained_transitions` never mints a transition on one. Fade it with
30	//!   opacity instead.
31	//! - **Blur, sharpen, pixelate and a blend mode.** The neighbourhood
32	//!   filters sample the layer's own texture around a pixel, and there is
33	//!   none; a blend combines a layer's colour with the canvas, and an
34	//!   adjustment clip has no colour of its own. `set_video`, `paste` and
35	//!   `paste_attributes` meet [`check_adjustment_video`] beside `check_blend`
36	//!   (errors, its precedent), and an action's end carrying one is closed by
37	//!   the evaluator ([`clamp_adjustment`]), as `clamp_video` closes a nest's
38	//!   blend.
39	//!
40	//! **On a matte track it is inert** ([`Project::inert_adjustment`]): a
41	//! matte group is one track, and two clips on one track share an instant
42	//! only in a transition, which is refused, so the clip could only be the
43	//! group's sole member and would act as an EMPTY matte. The recipe leaves
44	//! it out before the mattes are answered. On a track CUT by a matte it
45	//! grades only inside the matte, which needs nothing here: the compositor
46	//! weights its pass by the coverage like any matted layer's.
47	//!
48	//! Its stored transform, crop, corner, shadow, reflection, chroma,
49	//! spotlight, obscure and motion placement are kept and do nothing;
50	//! refusing them would make Paste Attributes fail from any moved clip.
51	//!
52	//! **The qualifier is its alone** (spec §11 GR-13): `video.qualifier`
53	//! narrows which of the destination's pixels the pass grades, read before
54	//! the grade. On any other clip a non-neutral one is an error in its own
55	//! sentence ([`check_qualifier_clip`], beside `check_adjustment_video` in
56	//! `set_video`, `paste` and `paste_attributes`); one reached through a file
57	//! or an action's end on another clip is inert, because the recipe
58	//! publishes it only in an adjustment source (`recipe.rs`'s
59	//! `layer_source`). Paste Attributes drops it onto a picture clip, and an
60	//! adjustment target keeps its own when the payload clip is not an
61	//! adjustment clip (`edit_paste_attributes.rs`'s `copy_group`).

97	    /// drops it before `frame_mattes` sees it.
98	    pub(crate) fn inert_adjustment(&self, instance: &Instance) -> bool {

100	            && instance.inside.is_empty()

105	/// Whether the clip is an adjustment clip.
106	pub(crate) fn is_adjustment(clip: &Clip) -> bool {
107	    matches!(clip.source, Source::Adjustment)

110	/// The one rule about an adjustment CLIP's video group: no neighbourhood
111	/// filter and no blend mode. An `Err`, as `check_blend`'s is, so `paste` and
112	/// `paste_attributes` meet it through `settle_video` and refuse the whole
113	/// paste. Any other clip passes.
114	pub(crate) fn check_adjustment_video(clip: &Clip, props: &VideoProps) -> Result<(), String> {
115	    if !is_adjustment(clip) {
116	        return Ok(());
117	    }
118	    for filter in &props.filters {
119	        let name = match filter.kind {
120	            FilterKind::Blur => "blur",
121	            FilterKind::Sharpen => "sharpen",
122	            FilterKind::Pixelate => "pixelate",
123	            FilterKind::Sepia | FilterKind::Noir | FilterKind::Vignette | FilterKind::Invert => {
124	                continue
125	            }
126	        };
127	        return Err(format!(
128	            "clip {} is an adjustment clip and cannot take the {name} filter",
129	            clip.id
130	        ));
131	    }
132	    if props.blend != BlendMode::Normal {
133	        return Err(format!(
134	            "clip {} is an adjustment clip and cannot take a blend mode",
135	            clip.id
136	        ));
137	    }
138	    Ok(())
139	}

142	/// adjustment clip takes one. A neutral qualifier passes on any clip, so a

144	/// [`check_adjustment_video`]'s), so `paste` and `paste_attributes` meet it

200	/// The evaluator's last line of defence for an adjustment clip (an
201	/// action's end is checked against the vocabulary, never the clip): a
202	/// blend forced to `normal` and the neighbourhood filters dropped.
203	pub(crate) fn clamp_adjustment(mut props: VideoProps) -> VideoProps {
204	    props.blend = BlendMode::Normal;
205	    props.filters.retain(|filter| {
206	        !matches!(
207	            filter.kind,
208	            FilterKind::Blur | FilterKind::Sharpen | FilterKind::Pixelate
209	        )
210	    });
211	    props
212	}
213	    /// `next_id` from before the call; these two ops mint two objects, so
214	    /// the promise has to say which is which — the TRACK takes `next_id`
215	    /// and the clip takes the one after it.
216	    ///
217	    /// The name follows `detach_audio`'s, the crate's other op that invents
218	    /// a track it was not asked for: `Track <count + 1>`, unique without
219	    /// renumbering anything above it. A track called "Background" would
220	    /// read better for one second and then be wrong, because the user is
221	    /// free to put anything else on it.
222	    pub(crate) fn with_back_track(&self) -> (Project, u32) {
223	        let mut next = self.clone();
224	        let track = next.numbered_track();
225	        let id = track.id;
226	        next.tracks.insert(0, track);
227	        (next, id)
228	    }

230	    /// How long a plate is: the caller's `duration`, or the whole timeline's
231	    /// length when it is absent (spec §6).
232	    ///
233	    /// The default is snapped even though every clip end already sits on the
234	    /// grid — a hand-written project file is the case that is not — and it
235	    /// floors at one frame, because a background of an EMPTY timeline would
236	    /// otherwise be a zero-length clip, which `validate` refuses and which
237	    /// is not a thing the timeline can hold.
238	    ///
239	    /// A duration the caller GAVE is refused rather than floored, which is
240	    /// `add_text_clip`'s and `add_shape_clip`'s rule for the same argument
241	    /// and the envelope's rule for a length (`edit.rs`): a negative or
242	    /// sub-frame length is a caller's arithmetic mistake, and clamping it
243	    /// would answer a bug with a clip.
244	    fn plate_duration(&self, duration: Option<Ticks>) -> Result<Ticks, String> {
245	        let Some(given) = duration else {
246	            return Ok(self.snapped(self.duration()).max(self.frame()));
247	        };
248	        let snapped = self.snapped(given);
249	        if snapped < self.frame() {
250	            return Err(format!(
251	                "background duration must be at least one frame ({} ticks), not {given}",
252	                self.frame()
253	            ));
254	        }
255	        Ok(snapped)
256	    }

258	    /// Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, running from 0 for
259	    /// `duration` — the timeline's own length when that is absent (spec §6).
260	    ///
261	    /// With `media`, the clip is shaped as `add_clip` would shape one of
262	    /// that file in every respect but its scale: the right source kind,
263	    /// audio props when the file has sound, and a FILL scale where
264	    /// `add_clip` takes a Fit one — the module doc argues that one
265	    /// difference. With `color`, or
266	    /// with neither, it is a canvas-sized filled rectangle with no stroke,
267	    /// at scale 1 — the rectangle IS the canvas, so there is nothing for
268	    /// Fit to do and writing the 1 outright keeps it exact whatever
269	    /// `fit_new_clips` says. Either way the clip is named "Background".
270	    ///
271	    /// A plate the user then re-colours in the inspector's Fill row is the
272	    /// whole of the "Solid Color" command, and it is also how a full-canvas
273	    /// GRADIENT becomes reachable: a gradient is a shape's fill, so the
274	    /// gradient background the road map asks for is this clip with a
275	    /// `set_shape` after it.
276	    ///
277	    /// `Err` for `media` and `color` together (they are alternatives, and a
278	    /// caller that named both meant one of them), for an unknown media, for
279	    /// a media with no pictures to show, for a colour outside 0–1, and for a
280	    /// duration under a frame — and, through [`Project::finish`], when the
281	    /// extra track or clip would break a reader cap. Never an identity: the clip
282	    /// lands on a track of its own, so there is nothing here to refuse
283	    /// quietly.
284	    ///
285	    /// A timed media — video or audio — IS clamped to its own length,
286	    /// whether the duration was given or defaulted to the timeline's (spec
287	    /// §11, D4-4). It reads [`Project::whole_media_length`], which is what
288	    /// `add_clip` gives a clip of the same file, so the plate ends where
289	    /// its file does and its segment plays at rate 1. What that paragraph
290	    /// used to say — that an unclamped plate "shows nothing" past the end
291	    /// of its media — was measured FALSE: the plan stretched a six-second
292	    /// file over a twelve-second plate at rate 0.5. An image plate is
293	    /// unclamped still, having no source bound at all.
294	    pub fn add_background(
295	        &self,
296	        media: Option<u32>,
297	        color: Option<Color>,
298	        duration: Option<Ticks>,
299	    ) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
300	        if let (Some(media), Some(_)) = (media, color) {
301	            return Err(format!(
302	                "add_background takes a media or a color, not both (media {media})"
303	            ));
304	        }
305	        let mut duration = self.plate_duration(duration)?;
306	
307	        // Everything that can refuse is decided against `self`, before a
308	        // track exists to leave behind.
309	        let (source, video, audio, shape) = match media {
310	            Some(id) => {
311	                let found = self.require_media(id)?.clone();
312	                let has_pixels = found.has_video || matches!(found.kind, MediaKind::Image);
313	                if !(has_pixels && found.width > 0 && found.height > 0) {
314	                    return Err(format!(
315	                        "media {id} has no pixel size, so it cannot be a background"
316	                    ));
317	                }
318	                let source = match found.kind {
319	                    MediaKind::Image => Source::Image { media: id },
320	                    MediaKind::Video | MediaKind::Audio => {
321	                        // A timed plate is held INSIDE its own file, by the
322	                        // same function `add_clip` measures a whole media
323	                        // with — so the plate's two `Err` sentences are
324	                        // that op's, and the segment plays at rate 1
325	                        // (spec §11, D4-4).
326	                        duration = duration.min(self.whole_media_length(&found)?);
327	                        Source::Media {
328	                            media: id,
329	                            r#in: 0,
330	                            reversed: false,
331	                        }
332	                    }
333	                    // Unreached: a LUT's row has no pixels, refused above.
334	                    MediaKind::Lut => return Err(crate::lut::lut_not_placeable(id)),
335	                };
336	                // FILL, not `add_clip`'s Fit: a plate that leaves the canvas
337	                // showing down one side has failed at the one thing a
338	                // background is for, and whether Fit leaves it showing
339	                // depends on `canvas.fit_new_clips`, which has no opinion
340	                // about backgrounds. The module doc argues it at length.
341	                let video = VideoProps {
342	                    scale: self.fill_scale(f64::from(found.width), f64::from(found.height)),
343	                    ..VideoProps::default()
344	                };
345	                (
346	                    source,
347	                    video,
348	                    found.has_audio.then(AudioProps::default),
349	                    None,
350	                )
351	            }
352	            None => {
353	                let plate = ShapeProps {
354	                    kind: ShapeKind::Rectangle,
355	                    width: f64::from(self.canvas.width),
356	                    height: f64::from(self.canvas.height),
357	                    stroke: None,
358	                    fill: Some(color.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PLATE)),
359	                    ..ShapeProps::default()
360	                };
361	                // The caller's colour reaches the same check a `set_shape`
362	                // of it would, so `[0, 0, 255, 1]` is named here rather
363	                // than blown out on the canvas.
364	                check_shape(&plate)?;
365	                (Source::Shape, VideoProps::default(), None, Some(plate))
366	            }
367	        };
368	
369	        let (mut next, track) = self.with_back_track();
370	        let clip = Clip {
371	            video: Some(video),
372	            audio,
373	            shape,
374	            name: Some(BACKGROUND_NAME.to_string()),
375	            ..Clip::placed(next.allocate_id(), track, 0, duration, source)
376	        };
377	        next.clips.push(clip);
378	        self.finish(next)
379	    }

381	    /// Copies `clip` onto a new back-most track, blown up to fill the canvas
382	    /// and blurred — the screencast backdrop (spec §6).
383	    ///
384	    /// The copy keeps the source, the in point, the start, the duration and
385	    /// the speed, so it plays the SAME FRAMES as the clip in front of it and
386	    /// stays exact under any later trim of its own; it drops its audio, its
387	    /// duck, its transition, its actions and its identity, and it takes a
388	    /// fill scale, a centred position, no crop, a `normal` blend and one
389	    /// full-strength blur. The module doc argues each of those.
390	    ///
391	    /// **A NEST clip is refused**, and it is the one refusal here that is
392	    /// not about a missing size — a nest has a frozen canvas and
393	    /// `Project::source_size` answers with it. It is about the BLUR.
394	    /// Flattening
395	    /// (`nest.rs`) folds a nest clip's PLACEMENT down onto the layers inside
396	    /// it and drops every per-pixel property it carries: a nest clip never
397	    /// becomes a layer of its own, so `recipe.rs::layer` reads `filters`,
398	    /// the colour controls, the chroma key, the shadow, the reflection, the
399	    /// spotlight, the hidden regions and the blend off the INNER clip and
400	    /// never off the nest clip. The blur this op writes would therefore
401	    /// reach nothing, and the command would report success having minted a
402	    /// SHARP 1.5× duplicate of the nest sitting behind the original, at
403	    /// double the render cost — a wrong picture answered with no message,
404	    /// which is the failure shape this crate refuses by name everywhere
405	    /// else. It is the same call `edit_props.rs`'s `check_blend` makes about
406	    /// `video.blend` on a nest clip, and `clamp_video`'s about an end patch
407	    /// carrying one; a blur is a per-pixel property like any other. The way
408	    /// in is the round trip the rest of the crate already uses for a nest —
409	    /// ⇧⌘G, blur the clip, ⌘G — and it is what `Frame`'s doc in `nest.rs`
410	    /// records as a limit of the flattening rather than of this op.
411	    ///
412	    /// `Err` for an unknown clip, for a nest, for a source with no pixel
413	    /// size — a text clip, an audio-only one, or a degenerate shape, which
414	    /// have nothing to scale to the canvas — and for a clip carrying no
415	    /// video properties at all. `Err` too when
416	    /// the extra track or clip would break a reader cap, which
417	    /// [`Project::finish`] reports through `validate`. Never an identity: a copy
418	    /// on a new empty track can neither be an identity nor break the overlap
419	    /// rule, so there is nothing here to refuse quietly.
420	    pub fn add_blurred_background(&self, clip: u32) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
421	        let target = self.require_clip(clip)?.clone();
422	        let (mut next, track) = self.with_back_track();
423	        let id = next.allocate_id();
424	        let copy = self.blurred_copy(&target, id, track)?;
425	        next.clips.push(copy);
426	        self.finish(next)
427	    }
428	
429	    /// The blurred copy of `target` with id `id` on track `track`: what
430	    /// [`Project::add_blurred_background`] places, and what `reframe_clip`'s
431	    /// backdrop places (spec §11 VR-25). `Err` for a nest, a source with no
432	    /// pixel size and a clip with no video properties, in that order — the
433	    /// op's own sentences.
434	    pub(crate) fn blurred_copy(&self, target: &Clip, id: u32, track: u32) -> Result<Clip, String> {
435	        let clip = target.id;
436	        if matches!(target.source, Source::Nest { .. }) {
437	            return Err(format!(
438	                "clip {clip} shows a nest, whose own filters the flattening drops, \
439	                 so a blurred copy of it would come out sharp"
440	            ));
441	        }
442	        let Some((source_width, source_height)) = self.source_size(target) else {
443	            return Err(format!(
444	                "clip {clip}'s source has no pixel size, so nothing can be scaled to fill the canvas"
445	            ));
446	        };
447	        let Some(video) = target.video.clone() else {
448	            return Err(format!("clip {clip} has no video properties"));
449	        };
450	
451	        let mut copy = target.clone();
452	        copy.id = id;
453	        copy.track = track;
454	        // The pair `detach_audio` sets, read the other way: this half of the
455	        // clip is the picture, and the sound stays with the original.
456	        copy.enabled = Enabled {
457	            video: true,
458	            audio: false,
459	        };
460	        // The one field of the audio group that is not about this clip's own
461	        // sound. `duckers` gathers a duck from the flattened timeline with no
462	        // test of `enabled.audio`, a mute or a solo, so a copy that kept one
463	        // would duck the whole mix — the clip it was copied from included,
464	        // since the copy is a voice on no track and the `others` filter has
465	        // nothing to exclude it by. A picture command may not change the
466	        // sound, and no rendered frame could catch it if it did.
467	        copy.audio = copy.audio.map(|audio| AudioProps {
468	            duck: None,
469	            ..audio
470	        });
471	        copy.transition_in = None;
472	        copy.actions = Vec::new();
473	        copy.name = Some(BLURRED_BACKGROUND_NAME.to_string());
474	        copy.label = None;
475	        copy.video = Some(VideoProps {
476	            scale: self.fill_scale(source_width, source_height),
477	            x: 0.0,
478	            y: 0.0,
479	            crop: Crop::default(),
480	            filters: vec![Filter {
481	                kind: FilterKind::Blur,
482	                amount: 1.0,
483	            }],
484	            // A plate composites with the CANVAS, never with a mode chosen
485	            // for the picture in front of it — over the default black that
486	            // mode is either destructive or inert. The module doc argues it.
487	            blend: BlendMode::Normal,
488	            // And it does not MOVE (format version 8). A backdrop that slid
489	            // in, spun or pulsed behind the clip it was copied from would
490	            // be two pictures of one recording disagreeing about where they
491	            // are, which is the visible half of the same mistake as keeping
492	            // the audio switch — and a slide would leave the canvas showing
493	            // down one side, which is the one thing a background exists to
494	            // prevent.
495	            motion: None,
496	            // A backdrop cut down to the person is no backdrop (CO-20).
497	            cutout: None,
498	            // Nor is one cut by the person in front of it (CO-52).
499	            behind_subject: false,
500	            // Drawn behind and sharp, so it drops the blur (CU-113).
501	            motion_blur: 0.0,
502	            ..video
503	        });
504	        Ok(copy)
505	    }
506	}
507	//! `relink_media` — spec §6, table "Tracks, markers, canvas, media", and
508	//! spec §11 #63.
509	//!
510	//! A relink points a media at another file: Relink… after the original
511	//! moved (spec §5.6), the missing-media sheet, or the tool. Given the new
512	//! file's PROBE — the descriptor `MediaImporter.probe` answers, minus `path`
513	//! and `bookmark` — the record takes its duration, size, rate and flags, a
514	//! file of another kind is refused, and every media clip of it whose window
515	//! now runs past a SHORTER file's end is held to it. Without a probe the
516	//! record is kept: Consolidate and the open-time re-anchor point at a copy
517	//! of the same file. A probe's `original` (spec §11 #228-O) replaces the
518	//! stored one, so a probe without one clears it, and no probe keeps it. A
519	//! probe never carries `color`, and a relink keeps the media's Camera Log
520	//! (spec §11 GR-16): it is the person's reading of the footage, which a new
521	//! path to the same footage does not change. A probe's `cursor` replaces the
522	//! stored one as `original` does (spec §11 CU-39). A probe never carries `speech`
523	//! either; a probed relink clips the stored spans to the new file or clears
524	//! them (spec §11 AU-116).
525	//!
526	//! Cut out of `edit_track.rs`, which keeps the media list's other two ops
527	//! and the two things this one shares with `add_media`: `MEDIA_KEYS` and
528	//! `check_media_fields`, so a probe is checked in the same words a
529	//! descriptor is.
530	
531	use std::mem;
532	
533	use serde_json::Value;
534	
535	use crate::edit_track::{check_media_fields, normalize_original, MEDIA_KEYS};
536	use crate::export::describe;
537	use crate::export_overrides::spelled;

539	use crate::outcome::Outcome;

543	impl Project {
544	    /// Points a media at a new file, and — given its `probe` — takes the
545	    /// file's facts (spec §11 #63).
546	    ///
547	    /// A `bookmark` of `None` CLEARS the stored one rather than keeping it:
548	    /// a bookmark resolves to the file it was made from, so the old one
549	    /// would point straight back at the file the user is replacing.
550	    ///
551	    /// Answers, in order: `Err` for an unknown media or an empty path; `Err`
552	    /// for a probe that is not an object, that carries a key outside the
553	    /// descriptor's (or `path` or `bookmark`, which are this op's own
554	    /// arguments, or `color`, which a relink keeps), that does not match the
555	    /// schema, or whose fields
556	    /// `add_media` would refuse; then a REFUSAL for a file of another kind,
557	    /// because each clip's source kind was chosen from it.
558	    ///
559	    /// A probed relink writes `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, the
560	    /// three flags and `original` (none in the probe clears it), then
561	    /// holds each `media`-source clip of this media — on the timeline and
562	    /// in every stored nest, orphans included — whose
563	    /// duration exceeds the window the file now holds to
564	    /// `duration_resnapped` (D4-4): on the grid, at least one frame, the
565	    /// frame floor winning for a clip whose `in` is past the new end.
566	    /// Everything else on the clip is kept, as `trim_end` keeps it; a still
567	    /// keeps its `at`; the overlap rule is not re-checked (D7-3).
568	    pub fn relink_media(
569	        &self,
570	        media: u32,
571	        path: &str,
572	        bookmark: Option<&str>,
573	        probe: Option<&Value>,
574	    ) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
575	        let old_kind = self.require_media(media)?.kind;
576	        let path = path.trim();
577	        if path.is_empty() {
578	            return Err("media path must not be empty".to_string());
579	        }
580	        let probed = match probe {
581	            Some(probe) => Some(read_probe(media, path, probe)?),
582	            None => None,
583	        };
584	        if let Some(new) = &probed {
585	            if new.kind != old_kind {
586	                return Ok(Outcome::Refused(format!(
587	                    "media {media} is {} media and {path} is {}: relink it to a file of the \
588	                     same kind, or import this one as new media",
589	                    spelled(old_kind),
590	                    spelled(new.kind)
591	                )));
592	            }
593	        }
594	
595	        let mut next = self.clone();
596	        if let Some(found) = next.media.iter_mut().find(|m| m.id == media) {
597	            found.path = path.to_string();
598	            found.bookmark = bookmark
599	                .map(str::trim)
600	                .filter(|given| !given.is_empty())
601	                .map(|given| given.to_string());
602	            if let Some(new) = &probed {
603	                found.duration = new.duration;
604	                found.width = new.width;
605	                found.height = new.height;
606	                found.fps = new.fps;
607	                found.has_video = new.has_video;
608	                found.has_audio = new.has_audio;
609	                found.has_alpha = new.has_alpha;
610	                found.original = new.original.clone();
611	                found.cursor = new.cursor.clone();
612	                found.speech = clipped_speech(found.speech.take(), new);
613	            }
614	        }
615	        if probed.is_some() {
616	            // Each list is taken out for the walk so a clip's window can be
617	            // measured against the whole project, the new record included —
618	            // `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap` pattern, every stored nest once.
619	            let mut clips = mem::take(&mut next.clips);
620	            next.hold_to_file(&mut clips, media);
621	            next.clips = clips;
622	            for index in 0..next.nests.len() {
623	                let mut clips = mem::take(&mut next.nests[index].clips);
624	                next.hold_to_file(&mut clips, media);
625	                next.nests[index].clips = clips;
626	            }
627	        }
628	        self.finish(next)
629	    }
630	
631	    /// Holds every `media`-source clip of `media` in `clips` whose duration
632	    /// runs past the window its file holds, through `source_window.rs`'s
633	    /// one re-snap of a media duration.
634	    fn hold_to_file(&self, clips: &mut [Clip], media: u32) {
635	        for clip in clips.iter_mut() {
636	            if !matches!(clip.source, Source::Media { media: id, .. } if id == media) {
637	                continue;
638	            }
639	            if let SourceBound::Timeline(bound) = self.source_length_on_timeline(clip) {
640	                if clip.duration > bound {
641	                    clip.duration = self.duration_resnapped(clip);
642	                }
643	            }
644	        }
645	    }
646	}

648	/// A probed relink's `speech` (spec §11 AU-116): the stored spans held to
649	/// the new file — a span starting at or past its `duration` dropped, an end
650	/// past it clamped — and `None` when none is left or the file has no audio,
651	/// so `finish`'s `validate` never refuses a relink over spans. The spans are
652	/// not detected again.
653	fn clipped_speech(speech: Option<Vec<[Ticks; 2]>>, file: &Media) -> Option<Vec<[Ticks; 2]>> {
654	    if !file.has_audio {
655	        return None;
656	    }
657	    let kept: Vec<[Ticks; 2]> = speech?
658	        .into_iter()
659	        .filter(|[start, _]| *start < file.duration)
660	        .map(|[start, end]| [start, end.min(file.duration)])
661	        .collect();
662	    (!kept.is_empty()).then_some(kept)
663	}

665	/// A relink's probe read as a media record, or the `Err` naming what is
666	/// wrong with it — the Interfaces order of spec §11 #63: not an object, an
667	/// unknown key, the schema, then `add_media`'s field checks.
668	fn read_probe(media: u32, path: &str, probe: &Value) -> Result<Media, String> {
669	    let Value::Object(fields) = probe else {
670	        return Err(format!(
671	            "a relink probe must be a json object, not {}",
672	            describe(probe)
673	        ));
674	    };
675	    for key in fields.keys() {
676	        if !MEDIA_KEYS.contains(&key.as_str())
677	            || key == "path"
678	            || key == "bookmark"
679	            || key == "color"
680	        {
681	            return Err(format!("unknown key \"{key}\" in a relink probe"));
682	        }
683	    }
684	    // Deserialized through `Media` itself, as `add_media` does, so the
685	    // probe's schema is the model's schema with no second spelling of it.
686	    let mut record = fields.clone();
687	    record.insert("id".to_string(), Value::from(media));
688	    record.insert("path".to_string(), Value::from(path));
689	    let mut record: Media = serde_json::from_value(Value::Object(record))
690	        .map_err(|e| format!("relink probe does not match the schema: {e}"))?;
691	    record.original = normalize_original(record.original);
692	    check_media_fields(&record)?;
693	    Ok(record)
694	}
695	//! Camera log on a media (spec §11 GR-16): `set_media_color`, the rules a
696	//! `media.color` obeys, and what the recipe and the plan publish of it —
697	//! written once for every door that meets it.
698	//!
699	//! - **The op.** `set_media_color {media, color}` sets a video media's
700	//!   setting, or clears it with `color: null` (an identity when there is
701	//!   none). `color` is read strictly ([`read_color`]): an object or `null`,
702	//!   only the keys `log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `peak`, `detected` and `pq`, each
703	//!   through serde's own vocabulary. `detected` and `pq` are import's to
704	//!   write, so the op refuses them; what the op stores always has `detected:
705	//!   false`, and an absent `gamut` is stored as the curve's first
706	//!   ([`LogCurve::gamuts`]). `peak` is a PQ file's override (spec §11 HD-12):
707	//!   `color` replaces the Camera Log and the override together, import's
708	//!   reading (`pq.file`, `pq.from`) survives every op, and `null` clears
709	//!   both, keeping the reading.
710	//! - **The rules** ([`Project::check_media_color`]), each its own sentence:
711	//!   the media is a video file, or an image whose colour is a PQ still's
712	//!   `pq` alone (spec §11 HD-20 (b)); the setting has `log` or `lut`, not both, or
713	//!   is a PQ file's `pq` alone; `gamut` goes with `log` and is one its curve
714	//!   takes; `lut` names a `lut` media of the project; `pq`'s peaks are within
715	//!   [`PEAK_MIN`]–[`PEAK_MAX`] and `from` goes with `file`. The op answers
716	//!   them as refusals; `add_media` (whose descriptor may carry a detected
717	//!   `color`) and `validate` (a file) as errors, as they answer every other
718	//!   field. The op's own: a `peak` only on a PQ file and in range, an image
719	//!   taking only a `peak` alone, and an asked `color` with none of `log`,
720	//!   `lut` and `peak` refused.
721	//! - **What draws** ([`Project::media_input`]): the recipe layer of a media
722	//!   or still source and the plan's video segment publish the setting as
723	//!   `input` — `{log, gamut}` or `{lut}`, and `peak` (the effective PQ peak)
724	//!   beside either or alone — and the app converts at step 0. The recipe
725	//!   layer of an image source publishes a PQ still's `{peak}` alone (spec
726	//!   §11 HD-20 (b)), and `null` for `{pq: {}}`. A `lut` that names no `lut`
727	//!   media publishes nothing of it.
728	//! - **Removing a LUT** that converts a media (`lut.rs`'s `remove_lut`) is
729	//!   refused naming those media ([`Project::media_converted_by`]), or with
730	//!   `with_clips` clears the conversions with the looks.
731	
732	use serde_json::{Map, Value};
733	
734	use crate::export::describe;
735	use crate::export_overrides::spelled;
736	use crate::model::{Media, MediaColor, MediaKind, Project};
737	use crate::model_media_color::{PqColor, PEAK_MAX, PEAK_MIN};
738	use crate::outcome::Outcome;
739	
740	/// The keys a `color` may carry: the setting's, `peak` (the op's alone), and
741	/// the two import writes, which the op refuses by name.
742	const COLOR_KEYS: [&str; 6] = ["log", "gamut", "lut", "peak", "detected", "pq"];
743	
744	/// An asked `color`: the Camera Log as the model spells it, and `peak`.
745	struct Asked {
746	    color: MediaColor,
747	    peak: Option<i64>,
748	}
749	
750	/// A media kind as a sentence names it: "an audio file", "an image", "a LUT".
751	fn kind_phrase(kind: MediaKind) -> &'static str {
752	    match kind {
753	        MediaKind::Video => "a video file",
754	        MediaKind::Audio => "an audio file",
755	        MediaKind::Image => "an image",
756	        MediaKind::Lut => "a LUT",
757	    }
758	}
759	
760	/// The sentence for a setting with nothing to convert by.
761	const NEEDS_LOG_OR_LUT: &str = "color needs log or lut; null clears it";
762	
763	/// A colour is a setting on a video file; on an image only when `image_ok`
764	/// (a PQ still's peak alone, spec §11 HD-20 (b)), and every other kind never.
765	fn check_kind(media: &Media, image_ok: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
766	    if media.kind == MediaKind::Video || (media.kind == MediaKind::Image && image_ok) {
767	        return Ok(());
768	    }
769	    Err(format!(
770	        "media {} is {}; Camera Log is a setting on a video file",
771	        media.id,
772	        kind_phrase(media.kind)
773	    ))
774	}
775	
776	/// A stored `pq` (spec §11 HD-12): `file` and `peak` within
777	/// [`PEAK_MIN`]–[`PEAK_MAX`], and `from` present exactly when `file` is.
778	fn check_pq(pq: PqColor) -> Result<(), String> {
779	    for (key, value) in [("file", pq.file), ("peak", pq.peak)] {
780	        if let Some(n) = value.filter(|n| !(PEAK_MIN..=PEAK_MAX).contains(n)) {
781	            return Err(format!(
782	                "color.pq.{key} must be {PEAK_MIN}–{PEAK_MAX} cd/m², not {n}"
783	            ));
784	        }
785	    }
786	    if pq.file.is_some() != pq.from.is_some() {
787	        return Err("color.pq.from goes with color.pq.file".to_string());
788	    }
789	    Ok(())
790	}

792	/// `color` read strictly: `None` for `null`, else the setting and `peak`, or
793	/// the `Err` naming what is wrong — not an object, an unknown key, a `peak`
794	/// that is not a whole number, or a value serde refuses (its own sentence,
795	/// naming the variants).
796	fn read_color(color: &Value) -> Result<Option<Asked>, String> {
797	    let fields = match color {
798	        Value::Null => return Ok(None),
799	        Value::Object(fields) => fields,
800	        other => {
801	            return Err(format!(
802	                "color must be a json object or null, not {}",
803	                describe(other)
804	            ))
805	        }
806	    };
807	    if let Some(key) = fields
808	        .keys()
809	        .find(|key| !COLOR_KEYS.contains(&key.as_str()))
810	    {
811	        return Err(format!("unknown key \"{key}\" in color"));
812	    }
813	    let peak = match fields.get("peak") {
814	        None => None,
815	        Some(value) => Some(value.as_i64().ok_or_else(|| {
816	            format!(
817	                "color.peak must be a whole number of cd/m², not {}",
818	                describe(value)
819	            )
820	        })?),
821	    };
822	    let mut setting = fields.clone();
823	    setting.remove("peak");
824	    serde_json::from_value(Value::Object(setting))
825	        .map(|color| Some(Asked { color, peak }))
826	        .map_err(|e| format!("color does not match the schema: {e}"))
827	}

829	impl Project {
830	    /// Sets or clears a video media's camera-log setting (spec §11 GR-16)
831	    /// and a PQ file's peak override (HD-12). `Err` for an unknown media or
832	    /// an unreadable `color`; a refusal, in the rule's own sentence, for
833	    /// `detected`, `pq`, a `peak` out of range or on a file that is not PQ,
834	    /// an asked `color` with none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`, or a setting
835	    /// [`Project::check_media_color`] refuses.
836	    pub(crate) fn set_media_color(&self, media: u32, color: &Value) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
837	        let current = self.require_media(media)?.color;
838	        // Import's reading, kept by every op: `pq` without the override.
839	        let reading = current
840	            .and_then(|c| c.pq)
841	            .map(|pq| PqColor { peak: None, ..pq });
842	        let stored = match read_color(color)? {
843	            None => reading.map(|pq| MediaColor {
844	                pq: Some(pq),
845	                ..MediaColor::default()
846	            }),
847	            Some(asked) => match self.asked_color(media, asked, reading) {
848	                Ok(setting) => Some(setting),
849	                Err(why) => return Ok(Outcome::Refused(why)),
850	            },
851	        };
852	        let mut next = self.clone();
853	        let Some(row) = next.media.iter_mut().find(|m| m.id == media) else {
854	            return Err(format!("no media with id {media}"));
855	        };
856	        row.color = stored;
857	        if stored.is_some() {
858	            if let Err(why) = self.check_media_color(row) {
859	                return Ok(Outcome::Refused(why));
860	            }
861	        }
862	        self.finish(next)
863	    }
864	
865	    /// The setting an asked `color` stores on `media` beside its `reading`,
866	    /// or (`Err`) the refusal in the rule's own sentence, in this order: `detected`,
867	    /// `pq`, a `peak` outside [`PEAK_MIN`]–[`PEAK_MAX`] or on media that is
868	    /// not a PQ file, the media's kind (an image passes only with a `peak`
869	    /// alone, spec §11 HD-20 (b)), and none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`.
870	    fn asked_color(
871	        &self,
872	        media: u32,
873	        asked: Asked,
874	        reading: Option<PqColor>,
875	    ) -> Result<MediaColor, String> {
876	        let given = asked.color;
877	        if given.detected {
878	            return Err("color.detected is written by import, not set".to_string());
879	        }
880	        if given.pq.is_some() {
881	            return Err("color.pq is read from the file at import, not set".to_string());
882	        }
883	        let peak = match asked.peak {
884	            None => None,
885	            Some(n) => match u32::try_from(n) {
886	                Ok(n) if (PEAK_MIN..=PEAK_MAX).contains(&n) => Some(n),
887	                _ => {
888	                    return Err(format!(
889	                        "color.peak must be {PEAK_MIN}–{PEAK_MAX} cd/m², not {n}"
890	                    ))
891	                }
892	            },
893	        };
894	        if peak.is_some() && reading.is_none() {
895	            return Err(format!(
896	                "media {media} is not a PQ file; only a PQ file takes a peak"
897	            ));
898	        }
899	        if let Some(row) = self.media(media) {
900	            let image_ok = peak.is_some()
901	                && given.log.is_none()
902	                && given.lut.is_none()
903	                && given.gamut.is_none();
904	            check_kind(row, image_ok)?;
905	        }
906	        if given.log.is_none() && given.lut.is_none() && peak.is_none() {
907	            return Err(NEEDS_LOG_OR_LUT.to_string());
908	        }
909	        let mut setting = given;
910	        if let (Some(log), None) = (setting.log, setting.gamut) {
911	            setting.gamut = log.gamuts().first().copied();
912	        }
913	        setting.pq = reading.map(|pq| PqColor { peak, ..pq });
914	        Ok(setting)
915	    }

917	    /// A media's `color` against this project; `Ok` for a media without one.
918	    /// Each sentence is the rule's own, in this order: the media's kind (an
919	    /// image passes only with an import's `pq` alone, spec §11 HD-20 (b)), a
920	    /// setting with neither or both of `log` and `lut` (neither is a PQ
921	    /// file's `pq` alone, which passes), a `gamut` without a `log`, a pairing
922	    /// the curve does not take, a `lut` that is not a `lut` media of the
923	    /// project, and `pq`'s own ([`check_pq`]).
924	    pub(crate) fn check_media_color(&self, media: &Media) -> Result<(), String> {
925	        let Some(color) = media.color else {
926	            return Ok(());
927	        };
928	        let image_ok = color.pq.is_some()
929	            && !color.detected
930	            && color.log.is_none()
931	            && color.lut.is_none()
932	            && color.gamut.is_none();
933	        check_kind(media, image_ok)?;
934	        match (color.log, color.lut) {
935	            (None, None) if color.pq.is_none() || color.detected => {
936	                return Err(NEEDS_LOG_OR_LUT.to_string())
937	            }
938	            (Some(_), Some(_)) => return Err("color takes log or lut, not both".to_string()),
939	            _ => {}
940	        }
941	        if let (None, Some(_)) = (color.log, color.gamut) {

title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
  tools="set_enabled"
/>

## Turn a half off

There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:

| Command | What it switches |
| --- | --- |
| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
| [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |

To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

## How the clip looks

---
title: "Tools: projects and history"
description: The agent tools that open, make, save, close and read a project, and walk its undo history, with every argument, answer and refusal.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools work on whole projects: opening, making, saving and closing them, reading one back, and stepping through its undo history. None of them takes `scope`, because none of them edits inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/).

<AtAGlance
  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'save_project', 'close_project', 'get_project', 'undo', 'redo']}
/>

Every tool takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. A path that names no open project is refused, and so is a call with no project open at all, which is told to call `open_project` or `new_project` first. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/) for how times are written, and [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the short `project` summary most answers carry.

## `open_project`

Opens a project and shows its window, as [double-clicking a file](/projects/open-a-project/) does. It takes a `.framejob` package, or any movie, sound file or picture. A movie, sound file or picture [becomes a new untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/) sized and rated to it, with the file as the first clip on track 1.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The file to open, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |

It answers the opened project's `project` summary, with `missing_media` in that summary when a file has gone. If the file is already open, Frame Job brings that project forward and answers `already_open: true` with its summary. That includes a movie already open as an untitled project.

It's refused when:

- nothing exists at `path`
- the file doesn't open as a Frame Job project
- you're opening the same file in a window and that open hasn't finished after 30 seconds. Call it again once the window is up.

A tool call never asks a question, so a file that would normally bring up the [ffmpeg offer](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) is treated as if you'd declined it.

## `new_project`

Makes a blank 1920×1080, 30 fps project and shows its window, as [**File ▸ New Project**](/projects/start-a-project/#start-a-blank-project) does. Change its size and rate afterwards with [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | No | Where to save it straight away, such as `~/Movies/Cut.framejob`. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft until `save_project`. |
| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |

It answers the new project's `project` summary, and `saved`, the full path, when you gave one.

A path another open project holds is refused and nothing is created. `close_project` closes that project first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced.

## `new_project_from_range`

Opens a stretch of the top-level timeline as a new project, moved to start at 0, as [**File ▸ New Project from Range…**](/projects/new-project-from-range/) does with the in/out range. The project you take it from doesn't change and gets no undo step.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | integer | Yes | Where the range starts on the timeline, in ticks. It's rounded to a frame, and a negative time is taken as 0. |
| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the range ends on the timeline, in ticks. The frame at `to` isn't kept. It must be after `from`. |
| `path` | string | No | Where to save the new project first. `.framejob` is added when it's missing, and nothing may exist there yet. Without it the project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "*name* (range)". |
| `project` | string | No | The project to take the range from. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

What's kept follows the sheet:

- A clip across an edge is cut there, on every track, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/) would cut it. Locked tracks are cut too.
- A transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end.
- Markers inside the range are kept and moved with it.
- Media nothing kept plays is left out.
- Each kept file's caches come along, so nothing is analysed again, and so do the graphics the kept clips draw, with every font and picture. [What comes with it](/projects/new-project-from-range/#what-comes-with-it) has the list.
- Media files are never copied. The new project points at the same files.

It answers `project`, the new project's summary, `carried` with the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` that came along, and `saved`, the path, when you gave one. The new project opens in front, so later calls with no `project` reach it. Name it by its path once it has one.

It's refused:

- while a nest is open. Call `set_scope` with no arguments first.
- when `to` isn't after `from`, once both are on the frame grid
- for a path another open project holds, or where anything already exists
- for a nest clip across either edge, because a nest clip has no in point and would replay from its start
- when nothing plays in the range
- when an edge would leave a transition inside the range too long for what's left of its clip. Move that edge further from the transition.

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first when the call names a `path`.

## `save_project`

Saves the project, as [**File ▸ Save**](/projects/save-and-revert/#save-a-project) does, and answers only once the package is on disk.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | The first time | Where to write the `.framejob` package. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Giving a path always writes there, as Save As does, unless it's the project's own file, which is a plain save. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to save. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

A project needs a `path` the first time, whether it came from `new_project` with no path or from a movie opened as a project. After that, leave it out and the project is written back to its own file.

It answers `saved`, the full path, and the `project` summary.

It's refused when a project that has never been saved has no `path`, and for a path another open project holds. `close_project` closes that one first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced. A save that takes more than 120 seconds answers that it timed out.

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first, and says so when the call would replace a file.

## `close_project`

Closes a project and its window, as [**File ▸ Close**](/projects/save-and-revert/#close-a-project) (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) does. It never writes the package, so call `save_project` first to keep your changes.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discard` | boolean | No | Close even with unsaved changes, losing them. Default `false`. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to close. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers `ok: true`, `closed` (the project's name), `path` (null for one never saved) and `discarded_changes`, which says whether unsaved changes went with it. A later call naming that path is refused, because it's no longer open.

It's refused when the window has a sheet open, whatever `discard` says, and when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` and `discard` isn't `true`.

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call this tool, because closing the project would close its own conversation.

## `get_project`

Answers the whole project as JSON, plus what the app holds outside it: the playhead, the selection and the in/out range. Read it first, because every other tool names things by the ids it reports. [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/) goes through it in full.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | string | No | The project to read. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

Its answer holds:

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | The project itself: `canvas`, `media`, `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `nests` and `next_id`. |
| `path`, `name` | Where the project is, or null, and what it's called. |
| `unsaved_changes` | Whether it has changes not yet saved. |
| `duration`, `playhead` | Its length and the playhead, in ticks. |
| `selection` | The selected clip ids. |
| `in_out_range` | `start` and `end`, in ticks. Only there when a range is set. |
| `scope` | The open nest's id, or null at the timeline. With a nest open, `scope_clip` and `scope_path` come with it. |
| `missing_media` | The ids of media whose file has gone. Only there when one has. |
| `graphics` | Every module in the package, with its revision, whether it compiles, and the clips it draws. |
| `note` | A reminder of how to read the rest. |

While a nest is open, `project` is that nest seen as a project. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## `undo`

Undoes one step, as [**Edit ▸ Undo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) does. Every tool that edits makes exactly one step, so one `undo` walks back exactly one call. The history is the project's, so a step you made by hand counts as well.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | string | No | The project to undo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers `ok: true`, `undone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.

It's refused when there's nothing to undo. The tools on [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/) make no step, so they can't be undone.

## `redo`

Redoes one undone step, as [**Edit ▸ Redo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) does. Any new edit clears what there was to redo, as it does in the app.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | string | No | The project to redo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers `ok: true`, `redone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.

It's refused when there's nothing to redo.

---
title: "Tools: playhead, range and selection"
description: The agent tools that move the playhead, set the in/out range, select clips and open a nest, none of which is an edit.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These four tools change what the app is looking at, never the project. They make no undo step, they don't mark the project as changed, and `undo` can't reverse them. `get_project` reads all of them back.

<AtAGlance tools={['set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />

Times are in ticks, 600,000 per second, and each is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Every tool here takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.

## `set_playhead`

Moves the playhead and seeks the preview, as [clicking the ruler or a transport key](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) does.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `t` | integer | Yes | The time to move to, in ticks. A negative time goes to 0. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers `ok: true`, `playhead` (the time it landed on) and the `project` summary.

`split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` use this time when they aren't given one. While a [nest](/mcp/nests/) is open, `t` is measured from the nest's own start.

## `set_range`

Sets or clears the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), as **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>), **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) do.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | integer | No | The In point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current In, or 0 when there's no range. |
| `end` | integer | No | The Out point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current Out, or the project's end when there's no range. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

Call it with neither bound to clear the range. A negative time is taken as 0.

It answers `ok: true`, `in_out_range` (`start` and `end`, or null when the range is cleared) and the `project` summary.

It's refused when the end isn't after the start. [`export`](/mcp/export/) with `range: "in_out"` writes only this span, and `get_project` reports it as `in_out_range`.

## `set_selection`

Selects clips, as [clicking one](/timeline/selecting-clips/) in the timeline or on the canvas, or **Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>), does. The canvas handles, crop mode and every inspector pane act on the selection, so this puts the app into the state you want to look at.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clip ids to select, replacing the selection. Leave it out, or pass an empty array, to select nothing. |

It's refused when:

- both `clip` and `nest` are given
- no clip has that id, at the timeline or in any nest
- the clip doesn't show a nest
- no nest has that id
- no clip on the timeline shows that nest. Name the nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`.

---
title: "Tools: media"
description: The agent tools that bring files into a project, relink and remove them, copy them into the package, and set a file's Camera Log, peak and speech.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools work on the project's media list, the files a project points at. A file on the list isn't on the timeline until a clip uses it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

<AtAGlance
  tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'consolidate_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech']}
/>

The media list belongs to the whole project, not to a nest, so:

- The five edits that take `scope` (`add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` and `set_media_speech`) answer that they have no meaning inside a nest when you pass one. It's there so the answer can say so by name.
- With a nest open and no `scope` passed, those same edits apply to the whole project, and the answer lists them under `document_ops`.
- Media ids mean the same thing everywhere.

Every tool here also takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. Each edit is one undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the `project` summary and the two ways an edit can fail to happen.

## `import_media`

Reads a movie, sound file, picture or `.cube` LUT and adds it to the media list, as [**File ▸ Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/#add-media) does. It isn't on the timeline yet. Place it with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The file, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers:

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `media` | The new media id. |
| `path` | Where the entry points. For a converted file, that's the copy. |
| `original` | The file you named, when the entry points at a copy. |
| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. |
| `duration` | The file's length, in ticks. |
| `width`, `height` | Its display size. |
| `fps` | Its frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. |
| `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha` | What it holds. |
| `note` | What to do next: `add_clip`, or for a LUT, [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/) with a look. |
| `project` | The `project` summary. |

A [WebM or Matroska file](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) is copied into a `.mov` first and named after the original. A file the [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) converts is recorded the same way.

A tool call never asks, so where the app would offer to convert a file with ffmpeg, this answers with the reason instead. Convert it from the app's window, or set Frame Job to always convert.

It's refused when nothing exists at `path`, or when the file can't be read. A file whose path is already on the list changes nothing, and the answer says so. The step is called "Add Media".

## `add_media`

Adds a media entry from a description you supply, with no reading of the file. Use `import_media` unless you're replaying a project's own JSON. Frame Job has no menu item for this tool, because reading the file is the app's job.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `descriptor` | object | Yes | The entry to add, as below. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

The descriptor is an element of `media` from `get_project`, without its `id`. Only `path` is required by name.

| Key | What it is | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | The file. A leading `~` is expanded. | |
| `bookmark` | A base64 security bookmark. | None |
| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. | `video` |
| `duration` | The length, in ticks. | 0 |
| `width`, `height` | The size in pixels. A file with pixels needs both. | 0 |
| `fps` | The frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. | `[30, 1]` |
| `has_video` | Whether it has a picture. | On for `video` and `image` |
| `has_audio` | Whether it has sound. | On for `audio` |
| `has_alpha` | Whether it has an alpha channel. | Off |
| `original` | `{path, bookmark?}`: the file a `.mov` copy or conversion was made from. | None |
| `color` | A video file's Camera Log, as `set_media_color` takes it, plus `detected`, and `pq`, a PQ file's `{file?, from?, peak?}` as `get_project` shows it. | None |
| `cursor` | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`: the cursor file recorded beside a video, with `in_picture` true when the movie's own picture already shows the pointer. Both `path` and `in_picture` are required, and it's for a video with a picture only. | None |

It answers `ok: true`, `media` (the new id), `path` and the `project` summary.

An unknown key is refused by name, and so is a value of the wrong shape. A picture with no width or height, a video with a frame-rate term of 0, an empty path and a negative duration are all refused. A `color` that `set_media_color` wouldn't take is refused too. A path already on the list changes nothing.

## `relink_media`

Points a media entry at a file that moved, as [the Relink… sheet](/projects/relink-media/) and the Media tab's row menu do. `get_project`'s `missing_media` names the entries that need this.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
| `path` | string | Yes | Where the file is now. |
| `bookmark` | string | No | A base64 security bookmark. Leave it out and one is made for you, so the next move is followed automatically. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

The new file is read as `import_media` reads one, and the entry takes its duration, size, frame rate and audio, video and alpha flags. What happens to the rest is on [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/#what-a-relink-keeps):

- A clip running past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. One that starts past the new end keeps a single frame.
- Camera Log and an HDR10 peak are kept.
- Saved speech is held to the new file, and forgotten when the new file has no sound.
- The cursor file beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the old one stays as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the entry's cursor file is cleared.
- A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a `.mov` first, and a file the ffmpeg step converts is recorded the same way. Either becomes the entry's new `original`, and any other file clears it.

It answers `ok: true`, `media`, `path`, `kind`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha`, `original` when there is one, and the `project` summary.

It's refused when no media has that id, when nothing exists at `path`, when the file can't be read, and for a file of another kind, such as a sound file for a video entry. The step is called "Relink Media".

## `remove_media`

Removes a media entry from the project, as [**Remove** in the Media tab's row menu](/projects/remove-media/) does. The file on disk isn't touched.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the clips using it as well, including those inside nests. For a LUT, clear the looks and Camera Log conversions that name it instead. Default `false`. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

A nest clip isn't a user of the file, so it stays even when clips inside it go. Any [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) setting that listens to the file is cleared.

It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary.

It's refused while clips use the file and `with_clips` isn't `true`, naming the clips. A LUT in use as a look or a Camera Log is refused the same way, naming what uses it. The step is called "Remove Media".

## `consolidate_media`

Copies every file the project references into `media/` inside the `.framejob` package and relinks the project at the copies, as [**File ▸ Consolidate Media…**](/projects/consolidate-media/) does. Afterwards the package is the whole edit. It can be moved or archived and still open with the original footage deleted.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | string | No | The project to consolidate. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It copies as many bytes as the footage weighs, so it can take a while, and it has no **Cancel**. Frame Job's window doesn't respond until it's done. A recording's cursor file is copied beside its movie.

Files already inside are left alone, and missing files are reported rather than guessed at. A file that can't be copied keeps pointing at the original, so the project always still opens.

It answers `ok: true`, `copied`, `bytes`, `directory`, `summary`, `failures` and `missing` when there are any, and the `project` summary. When every file it can find is already inside, it answers `copied: 0`, `directory`, `missing`, a `note`, and the summary, and makes no step.

It's refused when the project has never been saved, so call `save_project` with a path first, when the project references no media files, and when nothing could be copied. The step is called "Consolidate Media".

The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.

## `set_media_color`

Sets how a video file's camera log footage is converted to Rec. 709, as the Media tab's [Camera Log popup](/hdr/camera-log/) does, and where a PQ file's highlights roll off to white, as its [HDR10 Peak field](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) does.

Every clip of the file and its reverse follow the setting. It's converted before the chroma key and every grade, and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) keeps it.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The video's media id, or a PQ still's for `peak` alone. |
| `color` | object or null | Yes | What to set, as below. `null` clears it, but the key must be there. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

`color` is one of these:

| `color` | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `{log, gamut?}` | Converts with a built-in curve. |
| `{lut}` | Converts with an imported `.cube`, named by its media id. [`import_media`](#import_media) it first. See [Camera log from your own LUT](/hdr/log-luts/). |
| `{peak}` | A PQ file's peak, a whole number of cd/m² from 1 to 10,000. |
| `log` or `lut` beside `peak` | Both at once. |
| `null` | No conversion, which shows the log picture, and no peak override. |

The curves, and the gamuts each takes. An absent `gamut` means the first one listed:

| `log` | The curve | `gamut` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apple_log` | Apple Log | `bt2020` |
| `apple_log2` | Apple Log 2 | `apple_wide_gamut` |
| `slog3` | S-Log3 | `s_gamut3_cine`, `s_gamut3` |
| `vlog` | V-Log | `v_gamut` |
| `canon_log2` | Canon Log 2 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
| `canon_log3` | Canon Log 3 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |

An Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is set at import, and `get_project` shows `detected: true` in the file's `media[].color`.

Import reads a PQ file's own peak into `media[].color.pq`, as `{file, from}`: MaxCLL, or else the mastering display's maximum. When the file names neither, `pq` is `{}`, which means 1,000. `peak` overrides that reading.

:::caution
`color` replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so send both to keep both. `null` clears both, and the peak goes back to the file's own reading.
:::

It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary. The step is called "PQ Peak" when `color` holds only `peak`, and "Camera Log" otherwise.

It's refused:

- on an audio file or a LUT
- on a picture, unless it's a PQ still and `color` is `peak` alone
- for a `peak` on a file that isn't PQ, or outside 1 to 10,000
- for a `color` with none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`
- for `log` and `lut` together
- for a `gamut` without a `log`, or one its curve doesn't take
- for a `lut` that doesn't name a LUT in the project
- for `detected` or `pq`, which only import writes

## `set_media_speech`

Saves where a file's speech is. [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) ducks the mix by these spans, and [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) reads them too.

**Audio ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by Speech** writes them from the file's detected speech, and so does [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) with `duck.mode` set to speech. Call this only to give spans of your own.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
| `spans` | array of `[start, end]` pairs | Yes | Where the speech is, in ticks of the file played forward, sorted, with each end excluded. An empty list means the file has no speech. |
| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary, and `get_project` shows the spans as `media[].speech`. Spans equal to what the file already has change nothing. The step is called "Speech Spans".

It's refused:

- on a file with no sound
- for a span that starts before 0, ends at or before its start, or ends past the file's duration
- for spans out of order or overlapping. Touching is fine.
- past 100,000 spans
